title: NREMT & NJ Certification Facts
body:
> **Key:** Item counts, time limits and retest policy are set by the NREMT and change between cycles. Everything below is the current shape of the process — confirm the numbers in the current NREMT Candidate Handbook before you schedule.

## Cognitive exam format

| Item | EMT |
|---|---|
| Type | Computer adaptive test (CAT) — each item's difficulty responds to your last answer |
| Length | `70–120` items, including unscored pilot items |
| Time limit | `2 hours` |
| Delivery | Pearson VUE test center, or online proctored where offered |
| Result | Pass/fail only, no score. The engine stops when it is `95%` confident you are above or below the passing standard |
| Turnaround | Usually within `2` business days on the NREMT portal |

A CAT that shuts off at item `70` is not a bad sign. It means the engine reached `95%` confidence early, in either direction.

## The five domains

| Domain | Weight |
|---|---|
| Airway, Respiration and Ventilation | `18–22%` |
| Cardiology and Resuscitation | `20–24%` |
| Trauma | `14–18%` |
| Medical, Obstetrics and Gynecology | `27–31%` |
| EMS Operations | `10–14%` |

Across every domain, about `85%` of items involve adult patients and `15%` involve pediatric patients.

## Retesting

- Wait `15 days` between attempts.
- You get `3` attempts. After a third failure you must complete documented remedial training — a `24-hour` refresher covering the failed content areas — before testing again.
- That buys `3` more attempts, for `6` total. After `6` failures you must repeat an entire entry-level EMT course.
- National certification runs `2 years` and expires on `March 31` of the expiration year.

## Psychomotor

The NREMT has moved EMT psychomotor verification out of a centralized state-run exam and into the education program, which attests that you demonstrated competency. **Individual states still set their own practical requirement**, so what you actually sit for depends on New Jersey OEMS and your program. Learn the classic stations anyway — they are the shape of every practical you will ever take.

Stations: patient assessment and management (trauma), patient assessment and management (medical), BVM ventilation of an apneic adult, oxygen administration by nonrebreather, spinal motion restriction (seated and supine), bleeding control and shock management, long-bone and joint immobilization, cardiac arrest management with an AED.

Critical failure criteria, in short:

- Did not take or verbalize standard precautions
- Did not determine scene safety before entering
- Did not voice and then actually provide high-concentration oxygen
- Did not find and manage a life threat before moving on
- Performed any other assessment before airway, breathing and circulation
- Ventilated at the wrong rate or volume, or interrupted ventilations for more than `30 s`
- Did not control major bleeding
- Did not decide between immediate transport and continued on-scene assessment
- Did not reassess after an intervention
- Did not immobilize before moving a suspected spinal injury, or caused excessive spinal movement
- Did not check pulse, motor and sensation before **and** after splinting
- Ordered or performed a dangerous or clearly inappropriate intervention
- Showed unacceptable affect toward the patient, a bystander, or a crew member

## New Jersey certification

1. Complete a New Jersey OEMS-approved EMT course.
2. Hold a current CPR credential at the healthcare-provider level (AHA BLS or equivalent).
3. Pass the NREMT cognitive exam. National certification requires you to be at least `18` years old; New Jersey's age and junior-member rules are set separately by OEMS.
4. Satisfy the psychomotor requirement as New Jersey and your program define it.
5. Apply to New Jersey OEMS for state certification, including the criminal history background check and fingerprinting.
6. New Jersey EMT certification runs on a `3-year` cycle, while NREMT national certification runs `2 years`. Track both dates separately — they will not line up.

## Recertification: the NCCP `40 hours`

| Component | Hours | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| National | `20 h` | Topics the NREMT specifies for the cycle, allocated across the airway, cardiovascular, trauma, medical and operations areas |
| Local / state | `10 h` | Content your state or agency requires |
| Individual | `10 h` | Your choice — anything EMS-relevant |

The national component's exact topic-hour split is published in the current NCCP document and is revised each cycle. You also need a current CPR credential and verification from a state EMS office or your medical director.

## Exam-day checklist

- A valid, unexpired **government-issued photo ID with a signature**, with your name matching the Authorization to Test **exactly**
- Your Authorization to Test, valid `90 days` from issue
- Arrive `30 minutes` early; late arrival forfeits the seat and the fee
- Nothing in the room: no phone, no watch, no notes, no food or drink. Lockers are provided
- Expect a photo, a digital signature and a palm scan at check-in
- An erasable noteboard is issued — use it for the vitals and the rule-out list
- Breaks are unscheduled and the clock keeps running

## Decoding the cue word

| Stem says | It is asking for |
|---|---|
| **First** / **initial** | The very first thing in the sequence. Scene safety, standard precautions, or airway — nothing has happened yet |
| **Next** | What follows what has *already* been done. Reread the stem for what was completed |
| **Best** / **most appropriate** | More than one choice is correct. Pick the highest priority or the safest outcome |
| **Most likely** | The most probable diagnosis given the pattern, not the most dangerous one |
| **Priority** | The life threat. Airway, then breathing, then circulation |
| **Immediately** | The intervention that cannot wait even one more step |
| **Except** / **not** / **least** | A negative stem. Three answers are right and you are hunting the one that is wrong |
| **Should** | Standard of care, not what your preceptor does |

> **On the exam:** When two answers both look right, one of them almost always assumes something the stem never told you. Pick the one that works with only the facts on the page.
